inputs.original_text: It’s understandable that he misses the appearance of US-China unity, but international agreement isn’t an end in itself. A government’s first duty is to its own people, families, and national sovereignty—not to preserve a global treaty simply to satisfy diplomatic expectations. Trump’s withdrawal may disappoint advocates of the Paris Agreement, but standing apart from an international consensus can be a defense of national accountability, not a rejection of responsibility.
inputs.modified_text: There’s no virtue in keeping up an appearance of US-China unity if it means putting international expectations ahead of our own people. A government answers to its citizens and families, not to a global consensus. Trump’s withdrawal from the Paris Agreement was a defense of national sovereignty and accountability—not proof that America has abandoned responsibility. Countries should make their own choices, not outsource them to international institutions.
